2026-03.title: India Begins 100-Day Countdown to International Yoga Day 2026
2026-03.summary: The Ministry of Ayush and Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga are organizing Yoga Mahotsav-2026 on March 13, 2026, marking the 100-day countdown to International Day of Yoga (IDY) 2026. This initiative involves 100 organizations promoting yoga in 100 cities. The program aims to expand outreach, encourage public participation, and prepare for the 12th IDY, scheduled for commemoration at 100 iconic locations, inspiring holistic well-being through yoga. Preparations are gaining momentum.

2026-03.title: India Proposes Drugs Rules Amendment to Streamline Blood Product Viral Testing
2026-03.summary: India's MoHFW seeks public comments on amending the Drugs Rules, 1945, to streamline blood product viral testing. The proposed change aims to remove duplicate testing of finished products, as pooled plasma is already rigorously screened for HIV, Hepatitis B, and C as per global pharmacopoeial standards. This aligns regulations, rationalizes testing, reduces compliance burden, and upholds patient safety.

2026-03.title: TRAI Assesses Network Quality at Key Puducherry Medical Facilities
2026-03.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) assessed mobile network quality at key healthcare facilities in Puducherry, including JIPMER Medical College and Rajiv Gandhi Government Women and Children Hospital, during its February 2026 independent drive test. Findings covered voice and data services from Airtel, BSNL, RJIL, and VIL, crucial for operational efficiency and emergency communications. This assessment highlights the importance of reliable telecom infrastructure for supporting public health services in the region.

2026-04.title: NSO 80th Round Survey Shows Transformative Progress in India's Healthcare
2026-04.summary: The NSO 80th Round survey reveals significant improvements in India's healthcare access, marked by a threefold increase in government insurance coverage and rising institutional deliveries. Public health facility utilization has grown, particularly in rural areas, while median outpatient expenditure remains zero. These findings underscore the government's commitment to affordable healthcare, effectively reducing the financial burden of out-of-pocket expenses for citizens.

2026-04.title: India Shifts Focus to Combat Non-Communicable Diseases
2026-04.summary: Union Health Minister JP Nadda highlighted India's transition toward a holistic health policy to combat rising non-communicable diseases. The government is accelerating NCD control through expanded infrastructure and massive screening drives, having already screened millions for hypertension, diabetes, and cancer. The strategy emphasizes that 70% of NCD risk factors are lifestyle-driven, urging a shift toward prevention and healthier living.

2026-04.title: NHA Concludes Chintan Shivir on Digital Health
2026-04.summary: The National Health Authority concluded a two-day Chintan Shivir in Pune focusing on AB PM-JAY and ABDM. The event highlighted innovation and cooperative governance, showcasing Karnataka's online referral system and Gujarat's clinical governance mechanisms. The initiative aims to strengthen healthcare delivery through data-driven decision-making and digital verification, ensuring improved clinical appropriateness and cost efficiencies across various Indian States and UTs.

2026-04.title: NHA Holds Chintan Shivir to Accelerate Digital Health
2026-04.summary: The National Health Authority convened a two-day Chintan Shivir in Pune to review and accelerate the implementation of AB PM-JAY and ABDM. The event focused on preventive, technology-driven healthcare and unveiled new guidelines and the NHCX strategy. Officials aim to strengthen digital health architecture and build a future-ready workforce to streamline health claims and improve overall healthcare delivery systems.

2026-04.title: MoHFW Launches Clinical Workflow App for CHOs
2026-04.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched an ICMR-developed mobile application to streamline clinical workflows for Community Health Officers at Sub-Centre Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. Aligned with 12 CPHC service packages, the app provides structured decision-support tools and checklists for patient assessment. This digital intervention aims to enhance primary healthcare delivery, ensuring timely referrals and informed clinical decision-making nationwide.

2026-04.title: NHA Launches Auto-Adjudication Hackathon for AB PM-JAY
2026-04.summary: The National Health Authority has invited innovators to the AB PM-JAY Auto-Adjudication Hackathon 2026 to develop digital solutions for claims processing. With over 2,600 participants registered, the initiative seeks to leverage AI and automation to reduce manual workloads and fraud. The goal is to create a scalable, transparent, and future-ready framework to handle the high volume of daily health claims.

2026-04.title: Union Health Minister Marks World Health Day
2026-04.summary: Union Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda extended greetings on World Health Day, emphasizing the government's commitment to preventive and promotive healthcare. He highlighted the synergy between traditional wisdom and modern science, citing Ayushman Bharat and PM Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana as transformative initiatives. The Minister praised frontline healthcare workers for their dedication in making quality treatment accessible and affordable for citizens.

2026-05.title: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission Surpasses 90 Crore ABHA Accounts
2026-05.summary: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission has achieved a major milestone, crossing 90 crore Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts (ABHAs) in 2026. Growth surged from 14.7 crore in 2021 to 90 crore, with Uttar Pradesh leading at 15.3 crore. These 14-digit digital identities enable secure, consent-based health record sharing, with women accounting for nearly half of all registered ABHA holders.

2026-05.title: India Releases National Family Health Survey-6
2026-05.summary: The NFHS-6 (2023-24) reveals significant progress in maternal and child health. Institutional deliveries reached 90.6%, and antenatal care coverage rose to 95.9%. Full immunization coverage improved from 83.8% to 87.1%, while child nutrition indicators showed positive trends, with stunting reduced by 17% and severe wasting by 32%. The survey covered 6.79 lakh households across 715 Indian districts.

2026-05.title: India Launches Tobacco-Free Educational Institutions (ToFEI) Application
2026-05.summary: To mark World No Tobacco Day 2026, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava launched the Tobacco-Free Educational Institutions (ToFEI) pilot application. The digital tool monitors tobacco-free norms and prohibits sales within 100 yards of campuses. Initially piloting in Rajasthan, Meghalaya, and Maharashtra, the app facilitates self-assessment and reporting to protect students from nicotine addiction and ensure healthier learning environments.

2026-05.title: National Health Accounts Estimates 2022-23 Released
2026-05.summary: India's Government Health Expenditure (GHE) grew threefold from ₹1.30 lakh crores in 2013-14 to ₹3.85 lakh crores in 2022-23. GHE as a share of GDP rose from 1.15% to 1.43%. Notably, out-of-pocket expenditure declined from 64.2% to 43.4% of total health spending, while government spending on primary healthcare more than doubled to ₹1.4 lakh crores over the decade.

2026-05.title: India Intensifies Ebola Preparedness Measures
2026-05.summary: Union Health Minister Shri J P Nadda reviewed Ebola preparedness following WHO's declaration of a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. While India reports zero cases of Bundibugyo Ebola, the government has intensified screening at international airports. The ICMR and NCDC are on high alert for tracking and testing, with updated SOPs shared across all States and Union Territories.

2026-05.title: India Advises Travel Caution Amid Ebola Outbreak
2026-05.summary: The WHO declared the Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak in DRC and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May 2026. With high mortality and no approved vaccines, India advises citizens to avoid non-essential travel to DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. Authorities are strengthening surveillance at entry points to detect febrile illnesses from these high-risk affected areas.

2026-05.title: ABDM Achieves 100 Crore Linked Health Records
2026-05.summary: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission has reached a milestone of 100 crore health records linked to ABHA accounts. This represents a doubling of records from 50 crore in February 2025 within just 15 months. Over 450 public and private health tech solutions are now integrated, facilitating a secure, paperless, and interoperable digital healthcare ecosystem across various Indian states.

2026-05.title: India Showcases TB Screening Efforts at WHA
2026-05.summary: At the 79th World Health Assembly, Union Health Minister J P Nadda highlighted India's 'TB-Mukt Bharat' vision. The initiative utilizes AI-assisted tools, digital chest X-rays, and the 'Khushi' multilingual chatbot to enhance early detection. India is deploying decentralized testing systems to reduce diagnostic delays in underserved regions, aiming to build a resilient, people-centered health system for lung screening.

2026-05.title: ICMR and ICAR Launch SEHAT Mission
2026-05.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research and Indian Council of Agricultural Research launched 'SEHAT', a national mission-mode programme. This initiative focuses on agriculture-nutrition-health convergence to shift India from curative to preventive healthcare. The programme prioritises biofortified crops, integrated farming systems, and NCD prevention, aiming to translate agricultural advancements into measurable public health outcomes through a whole-of-government and whole-of-system approach.

2026-05.title: NHA Concludes AB PM-JAY AI Hackathon
2026-05.summary: The National Health Authority, IndiaAI Mission, and IISc Bengaluru concluded the AB PM-JAY Auto-Adjudication Hackathon Showcase 2026. Over 3,500 participants competed to develop AI-driven solutions for health claims adjudication to enhance transparency and speed. Winning teams received cash awards up to ₹5 lakh, with the NHA focusing on scaling these innovations to prevent fraud and improve programme integrity.

2026-06.title: Launch of SUMAN Roadmap 2030 for Maternal and Newborn Health
2026-06.summary: Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda launched the SUMAN Roadmap 2030, a strategic framework designed to transform maternal and newborn healthcare in India. Aimed at achieving Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, the roadmap addresses persistent mortality challenges in high-focus states through an evidence-driven, targeted approach. Anchored in the RMNCHA+N framework, it employs a comprehensive life-cycle strategy, integrating critical health interventions from pre-pregnancy through childbirth and the postnatal period. This initiative seeks to ensure equitable, high-quality care by combining national priorities with local realities to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality across all diverse geographies.

2026-06.title: Introduction of Samagra Shishu Bal Swasthya Karyakram (SSBSK)
2026-06.summary: The Samagra Shishu Bal Swasthya Karyakram (SSBSK) was launched to provide a seamless continuum of home and community-based care for children from birth to 36 months. By integrating Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC) and Home-Based Care for Young Child (HBYC), the program emphasizes brain development and survival. A key community medicine feature is the risk-stratified approach for 'At-risk' children—such as those with low birth weight or malnutrition—who receive intensified follow-up. This includes up to nine home visits in the first 42 days for newborns and eight visits up to 36 months for children.

2026-06.title: Evolution of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Guidelines
2026-06.summary: The Anemia Mukt Bharat program has transitioned into the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, shifting focus from mere prophylactic supplementation to comprehensive therapeutic care. The new operational guidelines introduce the 'T4 Strategy'—Test, Treat, Talk, and Track—to strengthen screening and follow-up. The expanded 7x7x7 framework now includes low birth weight babies as a new beneficiary group. Integrating 'Jan Chetna' for community involvement and 'Eating Right' initiatives, the program also launches a unified digital portal for tracking and analysis, ensuring a robust institutional mechanism to combat anemia through a continuum of care across India.

2026-06.title: India Expands QR Code Drug Traceability Framework
2026-06.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare amended the Drugs Rules, 1945, expanding Schedule H2 to include vaccines, antimicrobials, anti-cancer drugs, and NDPS substances. Manufacturers must now affix QR codes to packaging. These codes store nine key data elements, including batch numbers and expiry dates, to enhance the safety, quality, and authentication of the pharmaceutical supply chain across India.

2026-06.title: Launch of AIR SUVIDHA 2.0 for Ebola Screening
2026-06.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation and DIAL launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0 to monitor Ebola health risks at Indian entry points. Following the WHO's May 17, 2026, emergency declaration, the portal requires international travelers to submit a health self-declaration 24 hours before arrival. It tracks 21-day travel history and symptoms, enabling real-time coordination between health and immigration agencies.

2026-06.title: Union Health Minister Reviews TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan Progress
2026-06.summary: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda reviewed the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, noting that 28 crore people were screened and 20 lakh received preventive treatment since December 2024. X-ray screening increased 34-fold via handheld machines. With 1.7 lakh shivirs covering 1.2 lakh high-risk areas and 1.9 lakh volunteers, India's TB incidence declined to 187 cases per lakh population in 2024.

2026-06.title: India Strengthens Dengue and Malaria Preparedness for Monsoon
2026-06.summary: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda chaired a high-level meeting to assess national preparedness against dengue and malaria ahead of the monsoon season. He urged States and UTs to strengthen surveillance systems for early detection and ensure the adequate availability of medicines, diagnostic facilities, and hospital beds. The focus remains on strict adherence to prevention, diagnosis, and treatment protocols nationwide.

2026-06.title: India Strengthens Strategies for Leprosy-Free Vision
2026-06.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare convened a regional workshop in Chhattisgarh to achieve zero leprosy transmission. While India attained national elimination as a public health problem in 2005, transmission persists in endemic hotspots. Officials emphasized early diagnosis, periodic case detection campaigns, and expanding Single-Dose Rifampicin coverage for eligible healthy contacts to interrupt the disease's transmission cycle effectively.

2026-06.title: PMSMA Marks Decade of Care with Major Health Gains
2026-06.summary: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda launched celebrations for 10 years of Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyaan. India achieved a significant 86% reduction in maternal mortality, outpacing the global average. Key health indicators show institutional deliveries have risen to 90.6%, while antenatal care coverage has reached 95.9%, reflecting the government's commitment to ensuring safe motherhood and healthy newborns.

2026-06.title: West Bengal Joins Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY Scheme
2026-06.summary: West Bengal has become the 36th State or Union Territory to implement the Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY scheme. Following a Memorandum of Understanding signed between the National Health Authority and the state government, health assurance benefits will now extend to approximately 1.43 crore families. This landmark inclusion marks a major step toward achieving universal health coverage and financial protection for citizens.

2026-06.title: India Celebrates Decade of Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan
2026-06.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched nationwide celebrations on June 9, 2026, marking ten years of the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan. To commemorate a decade of safe motherhood, Union Minister J.P. Nadda released a ₹75 commemorative coin and a ₹5 postal stamp. The initiative continues promoting nine assured free antenatal care services to ensure healthy pregnancies.

2026-06.title: West Bengal Joins Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY Scheme
2026-06.summary: West Bengal is set to become the 36th State or Union Territory to implement the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana. A Memorandum of Understanding will be signed between the National Health Authority and the West Bengal government. This expansion of the world's largest publicly funded health assurance scheme aims to provide equitable and accessible healthcare for all citizens.

2026-07.title: SRS Statistical Report 2024 & MMR Bulletin 2022-24
2026-07.summary: ORGI released SRS Bulletin 2024 (Vol. 59-I) and Statistical Report 2024 (reference year 2024), plus the Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality 2022-24. National CBR is 18.3, CDR 6.4, IMR 24 (rural 27, urban 17), NMR 18, U5MR 28, and TFR 1.9 (below replacement). Sex ratio at birth for 2022-24 is 918. India MMR is 87 per 100,000 live births (down from 88 in 2021-23); Kerala is lowest at 24 and Uttar Pradesh highest among major states at 154. High-burden IMR outliers include Chhattisgarh (36); Kerala has the lowest bigger-state IMR (8).

2026-07.title: Measures to Control Monsoon-Related Diseases
2026-07.summary: The Government of India has strengthened surveillance and response for monsoon-related diseases (Dengue, Malaria, Diarrhoea, Leptospirosis). Key infrastructure includes 887 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals (SSHs) and 27 Apex Referral Laboratories (ARLs) for Dengue, with IgM kits provided via NIV Pune. Five diagnostic labs were strengthened under the PPCL programme. Integrated Vector Management (IVM) strategies include Indoor Residual Spraying, bed nets in high-malaria areas, larvivorous fish, and bio-larvicides. Real-time monitoring is conducted via the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP).

2026-07.title: Key Findings of NFHS-6 (2023-24)
2026-07.summary: NFHS-6 shows improvements in maternal and child health: institutional deliveries (90.6% vs 88.6%), ANC coverage (95.9% vs 92.6%), and skilled birth attendance (91.3% vs 89.4%). CPR increased to 69.1% with unmet need dropping to 8.5%. TFR remains stable at 2.0 (below replacement level). Child health gains include full immunization (87.1%), measles vaccine 2nd dose (71.8%), and a significant jump in rotavirus vaccine coverage (85.4% from 36.4%). Stunting (29.3%) and severe wasting (5.2%) have declined. However, lifestyle diseases are rising, with 30.7% of women and 27.3% of men (15-49 years) being overweight or obese, and an increase in high blood sugar levels among adults.

2026-07.title: Expansion of RBSK 2.0 for Childhood Health
2026-07.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched RBSK 2.0, expanding its framework to cover 38 common childhood health conditions. New priorities include non-communicable diseases (diabetes, hypertension), mental health, and behavioral concerns. Implementation is strengthened through additional human resources for Mobile Health Teams (MHTs) screening in schools and Anganwadi centres. The program utilizes a digital platform for tracking and follow-up of the preventive, promotive, and curative continuum of care. To improve community awareness, new IEC materials (booklets, videos, posters) have been developed and shared with States/UTs.

2026-07.title: Increase in Medical Seats and Improved Doctor-Population Ratio
2026-07.summary: The National Medical Commission (NMC) reported a significant increase in medical seats between AY 2023-24 and AY 2025-26: MBBS seats rose from 1,09,115 to 1,28,976, and PG seats nearly tripled from 31,185 to 86,360. According to the Indian Medical Register (IMR), there are currently 15,35,155 allopathic and 7,51,768 AYUSH registered practitioners. Assuming an 80% availability rate for both systems, India's estimated doctor-population ratio has improved to 1:778.

2026-07.title: ICMR-NIN Releases Policy Priorities for Healthier Diets in Children and Adolescents
2026-07.summary: The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (NIN)-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' (LFOF) Consortium released a policy document titled 'Priority Policy Actions to Promote Healthier Diets and Food Environments for Children and Adolescents in India'. Launched by NITI Aayog, the document provides evidence-based recommendations to improve dietary behaviors and food environments. The LFOF is a multi-institutional platform involving partners such as WHO, UNICEF India, FSSAI, PHFI, and Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL).

2026-07.title: ICMR-NIN Releases Policy Priorities for Healthier Diets in Children and Adolescents
2026-07.summary: The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (NIN)-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' (LFOF) Consortium has released a policy document titled 'Priority Policy Actions to Promote Healthier Diets and Food Environments for Children and Adolescents in India'. Launched by NITI Aayog Member (Health) Dr. M. Srinivas, the document provides evidence-based recommendations to improve dietary behaviors and food environments for youth. The LFOF is a multi-institutional platform involving partners such as UNICEF India, WHO, FSSAI, PHFI, and Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL).

2026-07.title: ICMR Transfers Indigenous Biomedical Technologies for Cancer and Enteric Infections
2026-07.summary: Under the 'Medical Innovations Patent Mitra' initiative, ICMR licensed three indigenous technologies to Indian manufacturers. Key transfers include: 1) SHetA2, a first-in-class targeted therapeutic candidate for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) and cervical cancer, licensed to Emcure Pharmaceuticals Ltd. 2) Two next-generation vaccine technologies against enteric bacterial infections, developed at ICMR-NIRBI Kolkata and licensed to Biological E Ltd. These transfers aim to translate government-funded research into affordable healthcare solutions.

2026-07.title: CDSCO Approves India's First Dengue Vaccine: Qdenga
2026-07.summary: CDSCO has granted marketing authorization for Qdenga®, the first recombinant live attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine approved in India. Manufactured by Takeda GmbH, it is indicated for individuals aged 4–60 years. The vaccine is produced in Vero cells using a dengue virus type-2 backbone and contains GMOs. Administration is via subcutaneous injection; the recommended schedule is two 0.5 ml doses administered 0 and 3 months apart.

2026-07.title: Update on National Immunization Coverage and Pandemic Preparedness
2026-07.summary: India has maintained National Full Immunization Coverage (FIC) above 90% for four years: 94.7% (22-23), 93.7% (23-24), 98.3% (24-25), and 97.9% (25-26). A nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched Feb 28, 2026, targeting ~1.2 crore 14-year-old girls across 36 States/UTs. Other updates include the launch of an Integrated Training Module for Primary Healthcare Teams at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (April 2026) and ICMR's network of 160+ Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories for pathogen diagnosis.

2026-08.title: Health Ministry Reassures No New Influenza Threat; H1N1 Shows Expected Seasonal Drift
2026-08.summary: Union Health Ministry, along with DHR, ICMR, and NCDC, is closely monitoring seasonal respiratory illness trends nationwide through 73 DHR-ICMR Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs). DG ICMR Dr. Rajiv Bahl confirmed there is no cause for panic. Circulating Influenza A (H1N1) viruses have been identified as A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like viruses. Hemagglutinin (HA) gene analysis places isolates in clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1—a lineage in continuous circulation in India since 2025. Observed genetic changes reflect normal antigenic drift, not emergence of a new or dangerous strain. Genomic and epidemiological surveillance continues; seasonal influenza remains self-limiting. Authorities urged adherence to standard respiratory hygiene practices.

2026-08.title: National Workshop on SSBSK Convenes to Strengthen Child Health with New Shaishav App
2026-08.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a two-day National Workshop on Samagra Shishu Bal Swasthya Karyakram (SSBSK) on August 24–25, 2026, at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, chaired by Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NHM. The workshop brought together State Nodal Officers for Child Health and ASHA from all 36 States/UTs to translate SSBSK Operational Guidelines into action, focusing on continuum of care for newborns and children up to three years. Key emphasis was placed on risk-differentiated care for early identification and intensified follow-up of at-risk newborns and children. The newly introduced Shaishav App was highlighted as a digital tool for tracking children, home visits, follow-ups, and referrals. The workshop aimed to strengthen digital monitoring and the continuum of care under SSBSK.

2026-08.title: Government Bans Chlorpheniramine-Phenylephrine FDCs for Children Under 4 Years
2026-08.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has restricted the manufacture, sale, and distribution of all Fixed Dose Combinations (FDCs) containing Chlorpheniramine Maleate and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride for use in children below four years of age. The move follows recommendations of an Expert Committee and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), which noted potential risks to young children and availability of safer alternatives. This extends an earlier 15 April 2025 notification (S.O. 1717(E)) that restricted only certain FDCs with these ingredients; the latest order covers all formulations. Manufacturers must display the warning, "Fixed Dose Combination shall not be used in children below four years of age," on labels, package inserts, and promotional literature. Issued under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the notification takes effect from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

2026-08.title: NLEP Review-cum-Capacity Building Workshop Held in Indore to Accelerate Leprosy Transmission Interruption
2026-08.summary: The Central Leprosy Division, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, organized a two-day National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) Review-cum-Capacity Building Workshop in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, on August 19, 2026. Over 70 participants attended, including the ADG (DGHS), DDG (Leprosy), officials from RLTRI Raipur and Aska Institute, State Leprosy Officers, CMHOs, and District Leprosy Officers from all 51 districts of Madhya Pradesh. The workshop reviewed the epidemiological situation, programme performance, and implementation gaps, emphasizing strengthening early case detection, contact tracing, timely treatment initiation and completion, prevention of disabilities, and intensified surveillance as key components of the last-mile strategy for Interruption of Transmission (IoT) of leprosy.

2026-08.title: National Workshop on Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Convenes; New AMB Digital Platform Launched
2026-08.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a two-day National Workshop on Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (AMB) on August 12–13, 2026, in New Delhi, with over 160 participants from all States/UTs and representatives from the Ministries of Education, WCD, Panchayati Raj, Youth Affairs, and Tribal Affairs. Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava stressed stronger convergence across health programmes. A new AMB Digital Platform was launched to enable beneficiary-level tracking, treatment monitoring, and timely follow-up. The workshop focused on implementing the revised AMB Operational Guidelines (launched by Shri J.P. Nadda on 29 June 2026 at CCHFW), shifting from supplementation-focused to a comprehensive approach centered on testing, case-based management, treatment compliance, diverse diet, and digital tracking using the 7×7×7 strategy. States/UTs were also recognized for strong AMB performance.

2026-08.title: Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Unveils 7X7X7 Framework with New Operational Guidelines
2026-08.summary: Government of India released new Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (AMB) operational guidelines at the 16th Central Council of Health and Family Welfare (CCHFW) meeting on 29 June 2026, upgrading the strategy from 6X6X6 to 7X7X7. Key components: (1) Hb saturation testing using Digital Invasive Hemoglobinometers; (2) Prophylaxis and targeted therapeutic management by anemia category; (3) Segregation of nutritional and non-nutritional anemia for case-based management; (4) Shift from T3 (Test, Treat, Talk) to T4 (Test, Treat, Talk and Track) via robust digital tracking; (5) Dietary diversification through Eat Right Approach with locally available iron-rich foods; (6) Whole-of-Government convergent approach with inter-ministerial convergence; (7) Jan Bhagidari communication strategy for community ownership. The 7 beneficiary groups include children 6-59 months, 5-9 years, adolescents 10-19 years, pregnant women, lactating mothers, women of reproductive age (20-49 years), and 0-6 month LBW babies. The 7 interventions span prophylactic IFA supplementation, anemia testing, therapeutic management, and more.

2026-08.title: Steps Taken to Promote Menstrual Health and Hygiene Under NHM
2026-08.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare implements the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme (MHS) under the National Health Mission (NHM) to promote menstrual hygiene among adolescent girls, with States/UTs supported based on proposals in their Annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs). MHS focuses on: (1) awareness generation; (2) access to quality and affordable sanitary napkins; (3) safe and environment-friendly disposal; and (4) counselling on safe menstrual practices. Sustained IEC activities are conducted through health facilities, community platforms, frontline health workers, digital dissemination, and adolescent-focused programme platforms. A Menstrual Hygiene Policy for school-going girls is implemented via coordinated State/UT action to ensure access to safe, effective, and affordable menstrual hygiene in schools. Monitoring under NHM is carried out through a multi-layered framework reviewing State-wise Key Deliverables against approved targets during NPCC meetings with all States/UTs. MHM is recognized as a multidimensional, inter-ministerial issue requiring coordinated action.

2026-08.title: Update on Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP)
2026-08.summary: The Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP) provides free haemodialysis to eligible patients via district hospital-based centres. As of 30.06.2026, PMNDP is operational in all 36 States/UTs, covering 751 districts (including 44 linked districts) through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535 haemodialysis machines. State/UT proposals are considered in National Programme Coordination Committee (NPCC) meetings, with approvals conveyed through Records of Proceedings (RoPs). The Union Health Ministry undertakes periodic monitoring through the Common Review Mission (CRM) and visits by senior officers; non-operational centres are flagged to States/UTs for corrective action. PMNDP is supported under the National Health Mission (NHM) as a supplementary health subject. State-wise cumulative data on dialysis centres, including those added in the last two years, is annexed. Public health and hospitals remain State subjects, with GoI providing technical and financial support for dialysis infrastructure strengthening.

2026-08.title: Government Steps to Reduce Out-of-Pocket Healthcare Expenditure
2026-08.summary: India's MoHFW is reducing Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) through multiple Centrally Sponsored Schemes. AB PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh annual health cover to over 12 crore vulnerable families. Ayushman Vay Vandana covers 6 crore senior citizens aged 70+ irrespective of socio-economic status. A total of 1.87 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAM) have been operationalized for comprehensive primary healthcare including preventive, promotive, curative, palliative, and rehabilitative services. Free Drugs and Free Diagnostics Initiatives have been rolled out nationwide. Key schemes supporting affordable healthcare infrastructure include NHM, AB PM-JAY, PM-ABHIM (Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission), and PMSSY (Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana).

2026-08.title: Initiatives for Care, Nutrition and Welfare of Pregnant Women
2026-08.summary: Government initiatives under NHM ensure maternal healthcare, nutrition, and welfare for pregnant women. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) provides completely free delivery (including C-section), drugs, diet, diagnostics, transport, and blood transfusion at public health institutions. Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) offers free quality antenatal check-ups by Specialists/Medical Officers on the 9th of every month. Extended PMSMA focuses on individual tracking of high-risk pregnant (HRP) women until safe delivery. Other key initiatives include SUMAN Roadmap 2030, Anaemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, Mission Saksham Anganwadi, and POSHAN 2.0. Implementation is supported by robust monitoring, technology-enabled governance, and community outreach for effective delivery of maternal health and nutrition benefits.

2026-08.title: NHA Achieves 25 Crore OPD Registrations Milestone via ABHA Scan and Register Service
2026-08.summary: The National Health Authority's Scan and Register Service (formerly Scan and Share Service), under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), has crossed 25 crore OPD registrations since its launch in October 2022. Nearly 4 lakh citizens use the service daily. The service is operational across 30,800 healthcare facilities in 36 States/UTs. Patients scan a unique QR code at facilities using any ABDM-enabled Personal Health Record (PHR) app, consent to share their ABHA profile, and complete instant OPD registration without paperwork. Leading adopters include Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir. AIIMS New Delhi tops the country with over 54 lakh digital OPD registrations. The service significantly reduces waiting times and improves operational efficiency.

2026-08.title: Government Strengthens Food Safety Enforcement with Expanded Testing Infrastructure
2026-08.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has outlined measures to strengthen food safety enforcement under the FSS Act, 2006. FSSAI has notified 259 NABL-accredited food testing laboratories, 24 referral labs, and 305 Mobile Testing Units (Food Safety on Wheels) for sample analysis. Under the SoFTeL (State of the Art Food Testing Laboratory) scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been upgraded to enhance testing capacity. FSSAI regularly reviews the performance and vacancies of Food Safety Officers across States/UTs via Central Advisory Committee and Inter-State Zonal Council meetings. Consumer awareness initiatives include the DART (Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test) Book and Food Safety Magic Box, promoting adulteration detection and informed food choices. Implementation remains a shared responsibility between Central and State Governments.

2026-08.title: Union Health Ministry Notifies Stricter Rules Against Fabricated Drug Data
2026-08.summary: The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare has amended the Drugs Rules, 1945 (via G.S.R 756 (E), dated 16th October 2025) to enhance regulatory integrity. The Licensing Authority is now empowered to debar entities from filing further applications with State or Central regulatory authorities for a specified period if they submit fake or fabricated data. This adds to existing penalties like application rejection or license cancellation. The process includes a mandatory show-cause notice and a provision for appeal. The amendment aims to ensure drug quality, safety, and efficacy are based on reliable scientific evidence, deterring misconduct that poses risks to public health.

2026-08.title: NJORT Deployed for Chandipura Virus Outbreak in Gujarat and Rajasthan
2026-08.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to Gujarat and Rajasthan to manage the Chandipura Virus Disease (CHPV) outbreak. The multidisciplinary team includes experts from NCDC, ICMR, and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD). The response involves the activation of the NCDC Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) and continuous surveillance via the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP). Objectives include investigating transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum, epidemiology, and vector surveillance to guide evidence-based public health interventions.

2026-08.title: Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission Recognized by WHO SEARN as Regional Centre of Excellence
2026-08.summary: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), under the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, was recognized by WHO SEARN as a Regional Centre of Excellence in Pharmacovigilance and Technical Centre in Quality of Medicines during SEARN's 10th Anniversary Meeting held in Kathmandu, Nepal, on 4–5 August 2026. SEARN, a WHO SEARO initiative established in 2016, brings together National Regulatory Authorities across the South-East Asia Region to strengthen regulatory systems through knowledge sharing, regulatory convergence, capacity building, and reliance mechanisms. Thematic working groups focus on quality assurance, pharmacovigilance, clinical trials oversight, regulatory preparedness, and medical device regulation. The IPC delegation was led by Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, alongside Dr. Jai Prakash, Dr. Robin Kumar, and Mr. Arvind Kumar, showcasing India's regulatory excellence.

2026-08.title: NFHS-6 Fact Sheet Indicators Finalized for Data Harmonization
2026-08.summary: The Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) has finalized the indicators for the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6, 2023-24) National and State/UT Fact Sheets. In line with the Government of India's Data Harmonization initiative, the TAC focused on key health and family welfare indicators to reduce inconsistencies across official data sources. Notably, anaemia estimates will be released based on ICMR's 'Gold Standard' survey. The TAC included representatives from MoWCD, MoSPI, NITI Aayog, and the Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India.

2026-08.title: ICMR i-DRONE Initiative Reduces TB Diagnosis Time and Cost
2026-08.summary: An ICMR study on the i-DRONE initiative in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, demonstrates that drone-assisted transport of TB sputum samples significantly improves diagnostic efficiency in remote areas. In collaboration with AIIMS Bibinagar and the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), the median turnaround time for diagnosis was reduced from 15 days to 5 days. Furthermore, mean out-of-pocket expenditure for patients decreased drastically from approximately ₹9,451 to ₹91, enhancing timely access to diagnostic services.

2026-08.title: AB-PMJAY Impact and Expansion Update
2026-08.summary: As of June 30, 2026, AB-PMJAY has authorized 12.69 crore cashless hospital admissions totaling ₹1.92 lakh crore across 37,413 hospitals. The scheme provides ₹5 lakh/family/year for secondary/tertiary care to the bottom 40% of the population. Key expansions include coverage for ~37 lakh ASHA/Anganwadi worker families (March 2024) and 6 crore senior citizens aged 70+ (October 2024), regardless of socio-economic status. National Health Accounts Estimates 2022-23 show a significant decline in out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) as a proportion of total health expenditure, dropping from 62.6% (2014-15) to 43.4% (2022-23). Card details are available at dashboard.nha.gov.in/public/card.

2026-08.title: IPHS Digital Toolkit for Public Healthcare Assessment
2026-08.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is utilizing an open-source toolkit and web-based dashboard (www.iphs.mohfw.gov.in), launched June 28, 2024, to monitor compliance with Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) 2022 across all facility levels, including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. As of June 26, 2026, 100% of public healthcare facilities have been assessed through the IPHS Digital Toolkit, with 64% scoring above 50%. The system enables real-time updates and data-driven decision-making to identify gaps in staffing, equipment, and diagnostics in PHCs and CHCs. Rural health facility staffing details are available via the HDI 2023-24 report.
